title: The Borrowed Harbor
premise: In 1899, Casper Winterbourne, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, is ordered to deliver a sealed letter to a magistrate — but curiosity and a stolen glance reveal it names the family that once sheltered him as conspirators in a smuggling ring they never joined. Torn between the company that owns his debt and the harbor folk who gave him belonging, he chooses to steal the evidence and run it past three checkpoints before New Year's Eve seals the case forever. Betrayed at the second checkpoint by the only friend he trusted, Casper gambles everything on the third, where the magistrate's own daughter — his first and only love — must choose between her father's law and the truth. The century turns with the plot exposed, Casper's indenture voided by scandal, and an unlikely found family claiming him at last on the docks he was never meant to call home.
about_author: Ansel Marchetti is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing port ledgers and indenture papers along the pearl coasts. Their fiction draws on the faded ink of real dockworkers' letters to give voice to those history recorded only as line items.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Three years of careful silence shatter when his employer hands him a sealed letter for the magistrate — and Casper glimpses the name inside: the Okonkwo family, who fed him through his first starving winter. He begins copying the documents by candlelight, torn between terror and loyalty. Emotional beat: the awakening of conscience; silence no longer feels like safety.

chapters.title: Two Coins for the Ferryman
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He steals the full evidence file and turns to Tomas, his closest friend among the company clerks, asking help crossing the second checkpoint at the customs house. Tomas agrees — too readily. The chapter ends with Casper handing over the satchel and watching Tomas walk toward the magistrate's door instead. Emotional beat: trust extended, then broken; rising dread.

chapters.title: What the Tide Refuses
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Casper fleeing through the storm-lashed harbor while Elena Vasseur, the magistrate's daughter, discovers her father intends to convict the Okonkwos regardless of evidence. She intercepts Casper at the third checkpoint, and in one breathless confrontation she chooses truth over blood, forging her father's seal to void the warrant. Emotional beat: love against duty, both paying its price.

chapters.title: The Harbor Keeps Its Own
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, New Year's Eve. The forged warrant unravels the conspiracy from above — the magistrate's superiors, not the Okonkwos, were the smugglers — and Casper's testimony voids his indenture. On the docks, amid fireworks and borrowed coats, Mrs. Okonkwo sets a fifth bowl at the table without being asked. Emotional beat: belonging finally given, not earned; home as choice.
